title: Career roadmap · Extension Officer
summary: A practical route from Home Science into community extension, rural development, women and child welfare, nutrition education, livelihood programmes, NGO projects, and government field-extension roles.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a 4-year BA Honours pathway where applicable. A 3-year BA route can follow the same sequence by moving the final-year milestones one year earlier.

about.label: Route check
about.text: Extension Officer is directly aligned with the Home Science (BA) course.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build Home Science foundations, community communication, nutrition, family-resource management, fieldwork and extension skills.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Specialise in rural development, nutrition extension, women & child development, livelihood programmes or community education.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress into programme coordination, field supervision, monitoring and evaluation, training and community-development management.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine extension expertise with digital outreach, data-driven programme planning, policy implementation and social-impact leadership.

blocks.text: If pursuing a 3-year BA

blocks.text: Scholarships / fellowships

Potential funding routes include UGC-supported scholarships, university scholarships, government schemes and development-sector fellowships. Income, category, academic-performance and programme-specific eligibility may apply. Check the current conditions and award amounts.
Sponsorship note
Government Extension Officer appointments normally follow departmental recruitment rules rather than employer sponsorship. NGO and development-sector employment sponsorship is organisation-specific.

blocks.label: Application pack
blocks.text: Academic transcripts, degree/provisional certificate, CV, statement of purpose, references, fieldwork evidence, project portfolio, passport, English-language test if required and scholarship documents.

blocks.label: Visa/job-offer note
blocks.text: A Home Science or development degree does not automatically qualify a graduate for regulated professional roles abroad. Check professional accreditation, programme-specific eligibility and post-study work rules in the destination country.
Career progression
Actual progression depends on the employer, recruitment system and specialisation.
PhD routes
After a relevant master's degree, possible research areas include:
A PhD is particularly useful for research, university teaching, policy development, extension research and senior programme-development roles.
2040–2046 relevance

Extension professionals will increasingly need to combine field engagement with digital extension platforms, community data, monitoring and evaluation, behaviour-change communication, climate-resilient livelihoods and technology-enabled public-service delivery. Strong professionals will be able to translate policy into practical programmes that communities can actually use.
